text: Git is a popular version control system that helps developers track changes in their code. One of its most useful features is branching. A branch lets you work on new ideas without affecting the main code. Developers often create feature branches to add new functionality safely. When the work is finished, they merge the branch back into the main branch. Before merging, teams usually open a pull request so others can review the changes. This creates a clear version control workflow: create a branch, make changes, review, and merge. Following this process keeps projects organized and reduces the risk of mistakes.
